name: Xi Jinping
role: General Secretary, CCP; Chairman, CMC; President, PRC — hosted Trump at May 14-15 Beijing summit; issued sharpest-ever direct Taiwan warning to Trump: 'Handle it badly, the two countries risk collision or conflict'; pressed Trump on limiting US arms sales, opposing independence, no senior US visits to Taipei; no joint communiqué on Taiwan issued; met KMT Chair Cheng Li-wun Apr 10, 2026 (first CPC-KMT leader summit in ~10 years)
quote: Taiwan is the most important issue in US-China relations. Handle it well, the relationship holds; handle it badly, the two countries risk collision or conflict. Taiwan independence is the chief culprit that undermines peace across the Taiwan Strait.

name: Lai Ching-te
role: President of Taiwan (ROC), 8th President — Jun 4: called on China to 'face up to Tiananmen 37th anniversary' as PLA recorded all-time non-exercise record of 32 sorties; Jun 6: PLA re-escalated to 22 sorties (2/22 crossing median); Jun 7: PLA pullback to 4 sorties, 9 PLAN + 7 official ships; Computex 2026: 'the world needs a stable Taiwan to deliver AI'; HIMARS NT$800M deadline MET May 31; Taiwan GDP forecast 9.64% (16-year high); Rubio Jun 3: arms 'under review' not paused; US FMS pause (Epic Fury/Iran) active
quote: The world needs a stable Taiwan to deliver AI. I sincerely hope that China can face up to the June 4 incident of 37 years ago, acknowledge the truth, soothe the pain, and open the door to reconciliation and dialogue.

name: Donald Trump
role: US President (January 20, 2025 – present); concluded May 14-15 Beijing summit with Xi Jinping; said willing to speak directly with Taiwan's Lai Ching-te (May 21); confirmed $14B arms package 'in abeyance'; US Acting Navy Secretary revealed May 22 temporary FMS pause for Operation Epic Fury (Iran); China blocked Elbridge Colby Pentagon Beijing visit as leverage over arms; Taiwan HIMARS NT$800M deadline MET May 31 — budget passed May 29; PLA Jun 1: 8 sorties (2/8 cross median), 7 PLAN + 4 ships
quote: I'm holding it in abeyance — it's a very good negotiating chip with China. Taiwan should cool it a little bit. I will make a determination. I don't want to put myself in a position where I have to comment on whether we'd defend Taiwan.

name: Joe Biden
role: US President (January 2021 – January 20, 2025)
quote: Yes. If in fact there was an unprecedented attack. Yes, we would get involved militarily to defend Taiwan.

name: Wang Yi
role: Director, CCP Central Foreign Affairs Commission; PRC Foreign Minister
quote: Taiwan is China's Taiwan. Any attempt to split China is doomed to fail, and will be crushed by the wheels of history.

name: Tsai Ing-wen
role: President of Taiwan (ROC), 2016–May 2024; First female Taiwan president
quote: Taiwan is already an independent country. We don't need to declare independence — we are the Republic of China. We are sovereign.

name: Nancy Pelosi
role: US House Speaker (visit Aug 2, 2022); retired 2023; triggered Fourth Taiwan Strait Crisis
quote: America's solidarity with the 23 million people of Taiwan is more important today than ever, as the world faces a choice between autocracy and democracy.

name: Kevin McCarthy
role: US House Speaker (Jan 2023–Oct 2023); met President Tsai at Reagan Library April 5, 2023
quote: America does not waver — we support Taiwan's democracy and will always stand with our friends.

name: Hsiao Bi-khim
role: Vice President of Taiwan; former de facto ambassador to US (TECRO); inaugurated May 2024 — issued May 6, 2026 statement calling defense budget a signal of 'Taiwan's will to defend itself' as 4th cross-party talks concluded without consensus, floor vote possible May 8
quote: The defense budget shows Taiwan's will to defend itself. Our relationship with the United States is based on shared values of democracy, freedom, and the rule of law — and it will endure.

name: Cho Jung-tai
role: Premier of Taiwan (Executive Yuan), May 2024–present; former DPP Chairman
quote: Taiwan's defense is not a burden — it is an investment in the values and way of life we cherish.

name: Fumio Kishida
role: Prime Minister of Japan (2021–2024); announced historic defense budget doubling
quote: A Taiwan contingency is a Japanese contingency. Japan must have the capability to counterattack enemy bases if attacked.

name: Wang Huning
role: Politburo Standing Committee; top CCP ideologue; heads Taiwan policy coordination
quote: National reunification is the shared aspiration of the Chinese people on both sides of the strait. It will be realized.

name: Adm. John Aquilino
role: Commander, US Indo-Pacific Command (INDOPACOM) 2021–2024
quote: The threat of a Chinese attack on Taiwan is much closer than most think — within this decade. We need to act urgently.

name: Lloyd Austin
role: US Secretary of Defense (2021–January 2025)
quote: The United States has an abiding interest in peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. We will maintain the ability to resist any resort to force or coercion.

name: Wellington Koo
role: Taiwan Minister of National Defense (2024–present) — NT$8.81B procurement budget passed 3rd reading May 29 (no opposition) — HIMARS (82 launchers, NT$2.8B), M109A7 howitzers (NT$3.9B), anti-armor drones (NT$1.8B) funded; HIMARS NT$800M payment deadline MET May 31 (Executive Yuan emergency reserve backstop); PLA Jun 1: 8 sorties (2/8 cross median SW/E ADIZ), 7 PLAN + 4 ships; HIMARS provides 300 km deep-strike capability against PLA missile platforms
quote: HIMARS gives Taiwan the capability to strike at PLA missile launch platforms 300 kilometers away. The Legislature has passed the budget — Taiwan has met the May 31 deadline and is proceeding with this critical procurement.

name: Hou Yu-ih
role: KMT presidential candidate 2024; New Taipei Mayor; cross-strait dialogue advocate
quote: Only through stable cross-strait relations can Taiwan achieve security and prosperity. Military confrontation benefits no one.

name: Ko Wen-je
role: Taiwan People's Party (TPP) leader; presidential candidate 2024; pragmatic cross-strait position
quote: Taiwan needs to be strong enough that attack is not worth the price — but also wise enough to maintain dialogue channels.

name: Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
role: President of the Philippines; expanded US basing access (EDCA); South China Sea tensions
quote: The Philippines will defend its sovereign rights in the West Philippine Sea. We will not yield a single square inch of our territory.

name: António Guterres
role: UN Secretary-General; calls for diplomatic resolution of Taiwan Strait tensions
quote: The Taiwan Strait is a flashpoint for global stability. The world cannot afford a military confrontation in East Asia.

name: Sanae Takaichi
role: Prime Minister of Japan (2025–present); defense hawk; reaffirmed Taiwan Strait peace commitment with Trump (Mar 2026)
quote: Japan and the United States share a commitment to peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait and oppose any attempts to unilaterally change the status quo. We have a direct stake in this outcome.

name: Raymond Greene
role: AIT Director (American Institute in Taiwan); de facto US Ambassador to Taiwan — 2025–present
quote: The Trump administration is asking all partners, including Taiwan, to raise defense spending to 5% of GDP. We support President Lai's goal of reaching that target by 2030, and we call on all parties to pass the special defense budget without delay.

name: Adm. Samuel Paparo
role: Commander, US Indo-Pacific Command (INDOPACOM) — testified to US Senate Armed Services Committee April 22-23, 2026 on Taiwan defense budget urgency and PLA military buildup
quote: We can't want Taiwan's defense more than they want it itself. It's not a chicken and the egg, because you're not going to get chicken or eggs if you starve the chicken. Taiwan must show the resolve to defend itself — pass the NT$1.25 trillion special defense budget.

name: Cheng Li-wun
role: KMT Chairwoman (2023–present); completed 6-day China visit Apr 7-12 — met Xi Jinping (first CPC-KMT leader summit in ~10 years); KMT led passage of NT$780B special defense budget May 8 (compromise between KMT's NT$380B and DPP's NT$1.25T) via KMT-TPP legislative majority — bill passed 59-0 with 48 abstentions
quote: The NT$780 billion plan covers current and anticipated US arms packages; it is fiscally responsible while demonstrating Taiwan's commitment to its own defense.

name: Francois Wu
role: Deputy Foreign Minister of Taiwan — key diplomat managing US-Taiwan relations; publicly expressed Taipei's summit fears: Taiwan is 'most afraid' of being 'put on the menu' of the Trump-Xi summit (May 14-15, Beijing); Taiwan confirmed to be top item on Xi's summit agenda as of May 2 reports; intensive US-Taiwan consultations ongoing seeking pre-summit security assurances
quote: What we are the most afraid is to put Taiwan on the menu of the talk between Xi Jinping and President Trump. The more we share a common national interest with the US, the more I think we feel comfortable that we will not be put on the menu.

name: Mao Ning
role: Spokesperson, Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs — responded to international concern over China's July 6, 2026 submarine-launched ballistic missile test
quote: This was routine military training in compliance with international law and international practice. It is not targeted at any specific country.

name: Lai Ching-te
role: President of Taiwan — responded to Chinese Foreign Ministry criticism amid Japan-Philippines EEZ talks dispute, June 18, 2026; separately expressed hope for swift US arms package approval
quote: Taiwan's safeguarding of its own national security, its refusal to accept unification, and its refusal to accept rule by the Chinese Communist Party should not be seen as a provocation against China. We also hope the arms purchases can be approved as soon as possible.

name: Wellington Koo
role: Taiwan Minister of National Defense — warned of shrinking warning time against a potential Chinese attack, June 24, 2026, drawing on lessons from the US-led Resolute Dragon exercise
quote: Our response time to a Chinese attack is shrinking. Taiwan must draw the right lessons from allied exercises and accelerate our own readiness accordingly.
